items.title: Maersk is opening a 617,000-square-foot fulfillment hub in Hopedale
items.description: Maersk announced a $100 million fulfillment hub in Hopedale that is scheduled to begin operations in late August 2026 and create approximately 1,000 jobs. A facility of this scale can create substantial recurring demand across operations and facility-support categories.

items.title: Walmart won approval for a new Newton microfulfillment facility
items.description: Newton's Zoning Board of Appeals approved a variance allowing Walmart to move forward with an approximately 20,000-square-foot microfulfillment center in Auburndale. The project is planned as a Walmart Depot for online-order storage and rapid local delivery rather than a customer-facing store.
why: Fulfillment operations can create recurring site-service needs

items.title: Boston Dynamics is developing a 330,000-square-foot Waltham robotics center
items.description: Massachusetts economic-development officials reported that Boston Dynamics will renovate and develop approximately 330,000 square feet in Waltham for a mobility and robotics center, consolidate manufacturing operations, invest $100 million, and create 1,250 jobs by 2030. The project is a strong future-facing facility and operations signal, not evidence of a specific open vendor request.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: 42 North Dental is relocating its home office from Waltham to downtown Boston
items.description: 42 North Dental is moving its home office from 200 Fifth Avenue in Waltham to 99 Summer Street in Boston. The company says the new office will be ready for team members on August 26. A headquarters move can create near-term workplace and facility-support opportunities, though no specific vendor request has been announced.
why: Headquarters relocation with a specific August 26 opening date
Move-in and ongoing workplace-service categories are plausible

items.title: Wonder has two more Massachusetts openings scheduled for late August
items.description: Wonder's published Massachusetts expansion schedule lists a Millbury opening for August 20 and a Brookline opening for August 27. The two upcoming food-service locations create near-term prospecting signals for recurring operating and facility vendors, although vendor demand is not confirmed.
why: Two Massachusetts openings scheduled within two weeks

items.title: Game Show Battle Rooms is opening at Burlington Mall on August 21
items.description: Game Show Battle Rooms announced that its Burlington Mall location is scheduled to open for business on August 21. The entertainment venue is a new customer-facing operation and may create recurring local facility, event, security, and marketing needs, though no purchasing request is confirmed.
why: Recurring facility and event-service categories are plausible

items.title: ALDI opened a new Lynn grocery store
items.description: ALDI lists 126 Boston Street in Lynn among its current Massachusetts grand openings. A newly opened grocery location can create near-term recurring facility and operating-service opportunities, though no specific vendor need has been announced.
why: New Massachusetts store opened this month

items.title: Cape Cod Coffee plans an August Framingham opening
items.description: Cape Cod Coffee plans to open a new Framingham location in August 2026 as part of its expansion off Cape Cod. The upcoming opening remains a timely signal for local operating and facility vendors.
why: New physical location scheduled for August
Established operator entering a new market
Food-service operations create recurring vendor categories

items.title: CBSET is building a new Waltham research and innovation facility
items.description: CBSET says it is building new research and innovation facilities exceeding 100,000 square feet in Waltham, scheduled to open in Q4 2026. The move from its current Lexington-area footprint creates a sizeable upcoming facility and operational-services signal, though specific purchasing needs have not been announced.
why: More than 100,000 square feet of new research space
Specialized biomedical operations can require recurring site support

items.title: Field AI is expanding with a dedicated Cambridge robot testing center
items.business: Field AI / AI for Humanity Inc.
items.description: Massachusetts economic-development officials reported that Field AI is expanding its local R&D operations through a multi-phase investment that includes leasing a 20,000-to-25,000-square-foot facility for a dedicated robot testing and development center and creating 36 full-time jobs. Specific vendor needs have not been announced.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Industrious is opening a new Arlington Street workspace in Boston
items.description: Industrious announced that its eighth Boston location, the city's first under its smaller flexible-office Indy brand, is opening in August at 75 Arlington Street. The company now lists the location on its Boston workspace directory.
why: New Boston location opening this month

items.title: BoostBerry is opening a Harvard Square storefront this August
items.description: BoostBerry Açaí & Smoothies plans to open a Harvard Square storefront at 99 Mount Auburn Street in August. The new food-service location is a timely local prospecting signal for recurring operating and facility services, but it does not indicate a confirmed open vendor request.
why: New Cambridge storefront planned for this month
Recurring local vendor categories are plausible

items.title: Sky Nutro is investing $12 million to expand in Milford
items.description: Massachusetts economic-development officials reported that Sky Nutro selected a Milford site after a multi-state search and plans a $12 million expansion that will create 120 jobs. The food and nutrition manufacturing project can create future facility, industrial, staffing, and operating-service opportunities, though no specific purchasing request is stated.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Thyme Lebanese Street Cafe is scheduled to open in Harvard Square this month
items.description: Boston.com reported that Thyme Lebanese Street Cafe is scheduled to open in August at 1 Brattle Square in Cambridge. The 13-seat quick-service bakery and cafe represents a timely small-business prospect for local operating vendors, without evidence of any specific open purchasing request.
why: New Cambridge food-service location scheduled for August

items.title: Mass Cabinets plans new manufacturing and office space in Methuen
items.description: Massachusetts economic-development officials reported that Mass Cabinets plans to construct approximately 12,000 square feet of manufacturing and office space, add storage and equipment, and hire 25 new employees. The physical expansion can create project and recurring vendor needs.
why: New manufacturing and office construction planned
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Blue Collar Customs is expanding into a 100,000-square-foot facility
items.description: Massachusetts economic-development officials reported that Blue Collar Customs will expand from a 12,000-square-foot site into a new 100,000-square-foot building and add 18 employees. The sizable facility expansion can create demand for move-in, facility and operating vendors.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development
